title: STATUS OF EMRSs
body_text:
The Union Minister of Tribal Affairs Shri Jual Oram today laid a statement on the Table of the House that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs is implementing the scheme of Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) for providing quality education to tribal students in their own environment preserving local art and culture. EMRS are established in tribal dominated blocks having more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons, as per Census 2011. As on date, 728 EMRSs have been approved out of which 508 are functional across the country having 156593 students enrolled during the Academic Session 2025-26. In the State of Telangana 23 EMRSs have been sanctioned and all of them are functional with10199 students enrolled during the Academic Session 2025-26. Various steps have been undertaken to enhance the quality of education and sports facilities in EMRSs across the country such as well-equipped classrooms with modern teaching aids, bridge courses, remedial classes science and computer laboratories, libraries with diverse learning resources, playgrounds and sports equipment, facilities for extracurricular activities like music, art, and sports, smart classrooms for digital education, computer labs with internet access, skill development and vocational training programs on a pparel, Automotive, AR/VR, AI, Beauty & Wellness, Agriculture, Electronics, and retail to enhance employability, etc. The preservation and promotion of tribal culture, language and traditional knowledge are integral to the objective of Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) Scheme. To achieve this, Tribal Corners have been established in EMRSs to showcase and preserve the culture, traditions, art, crafts and heritage of tribal communities. Cultural Programs, Meets and workshops are organized to provide a platform for students to learn about, appreciate and celebrate the diverse tribal cultures and traditions of the country. Further, Regional Language Teachers are recruited in EMRSs enabling students to learn and preserve their regional languages. The Status of schools sanctioned and operational under the EMRS scheme in the State of Telangana is given at Annexure.

enrichment.summary: The Union Minister of Tribal Affairs, Shri Jual Oram, informed the Lok Sabha that 728 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs) have been approved nationwide, of which 508 are functional with 156,593 students enrolled in academic year 2025-26. In Telangana, all 23 sanctioned EMRSs are functional, enrolling 10,199 students. The statement also detailed quality-enhancement measures including smart classrooms, science/computer labs, vocational training, and cultural preservation initiatives like Tribal Corners and regional language teachers.
enrichment.context:
The EMRS scheme, launched to provide quality residential education to Scheduled Tribe (ST) students, mirrors the Navodaya Vidyalaya model but is tailored for tribal-dominated areas. Under revised norms, EMRSs are mandated in every block with more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons (as per Census 2011), reflecting the government's push post-2018 to scale up the scheme significantly from earlier decades when only a handful of schools existed since the scheme's inception in 1997-98. This is part of the broader constitutional and policy commitment to tribal welfare under Article 46, which directs the State to promote educational and economic interests of Scheduled Tribes, and complements other tribal development interventions like Van Dhan Vikas Yojana and PM-JANMAN.

The emphasis on vocational training in emerging sectors (AI, AR/VR, electronics) alongside cultural preservation (Tribal Corners, regional language teachers) reflects a dual policy objective: enhancing employability of tribal youth while safeguarding indigenous culture and identity, addressing concerns that mainstream education often erodes tribal linguistic and cultural heritage. However, the gap between approved (728) and functional (508) schools highlights persistent implementation challenges in remote, difficult-to-access tribal terrains, including land acquisition, construction delays, and teacher recruitment—issues that have been raised in parliamentary and CAG scrutiny in the past.

prelims_questions.question: As per the criteria for establishing Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRSs), which of the following conditions must a block satisfy, based on Census 2011 data?
options: More than 25% ST population and at least 10,000 tribal persons
More than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons
More than 40% ST population and at least 15,000 tribal persons
More than 60% ST population and at least 25,000 tribal persons
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that EMRSs are established in tribal-dominated blocks having more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons, as per Census 2011.

prelims_questions.question: Which Ministry administers the Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) Scheme?
options: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
prelims_questions.explanation: The release clearly states that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs is implementing the EMRS scheme.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the objectives and significance of the Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) Scheme in promoting the educational and cultural development of tribal communities in India. What are the key implementation challenges?
Examine the role of residential school models like EMRS in balancing modern skill development with the preservation of indigenous tribal culture and languages.
